baseline: Measured on this host (Linux 6.8.0-124, pinned LTP 20260529 prebuilt copied out of the Nix store): mkdir02 = 1 pass / 0 fail / 0 broken. Re-run inside a mount namespace with the guest's own /etc/passwd + /etc/group bind-mounted, it still passes and reports 'Found unused GID 2', confirming free_gid=2 in the guest's group table (root:0, daemon:1, users:100, nogroup:65534; tst_get_free_gid skips nobody's 65534 and takes the first unused id from 1, i.e. 2). Per assertion, with parent testdir1 = mode 02777 gid 2 and the creating process dropped to nobody (fsuid/fsgid 65534): (1) stat(testdir1/testdir2).st_gid == 2, i.e. the PARENT's gid, not the creator's fsgid; (2) that dir's mode contains S_ISGID, i.e. 02777 not 0777. A purpose-built probe (/tmp/isgid_probe.c) measured the whole rule on the same host, including the branches mkdir02 does not cover: in an S_ISGID parent (gid 11) a creator with fsgid 65534 gets dir -> gid 11 + S_ISGID set; regular file created 0777 -> gid 11 but S_ISGID NOT set; regular file created 02777 -> gid 11 and the requested S_ISGID STRIPPED (creator is not in group 11 and lacks CAP_FSETID); mknod fifo -> gid 11, no S_ISGID. In a parent WITHOUT S_ISGID (gid 11): dir and file both get gid 65534 (the creator's fsgid) and no S_ISGID. Gid inheritance is unconditional -- no group-membership or capability check gates it, only the S_ISGID-on-parent test.
failing_assertion: Asterinas: 0 passed / 2 failed / 0 broken (qemu.log 'mkdir02: fail (0.015s)'). Broken=0 proves setup() completed, so the parent really did take mode 02777 and gid 2 via SAFE_CHMOD/SAFE_CHOWN, and the two failures are exactly the test's two checks. mkdir02.c:31-36 'New dir FAILED to inherit GID: has <fsgid>, expected 2' -- the new dir's st_gid is the creator's fsgid (65534, nobody) instead of the parent's 2; and mkdir02.c:38-41 'New dir FAILED to inherit S_ISGID' -- the new dir's mode is 0777, S_ISGID clear. Note: the two wrong values are derived from the code plus the guest's /etc/group rather than read off a verbose log, because KIRK_VERBOSE is read by test/initramfs/src/conformance/ltp/run_ltp_test.sh:23 but is not plumbed through the Makefile to the guest cmdline, so kirk suppresses per-case stdout. The failure count of 2 and Broken=0 corroborate the derivation.
root_cause: The S_ISGID inheritance rule is absent from the entire fs tree, so no layer ever looks at the parent directory when initialising a new inode's gid and mode. On the tested path (CONFORMANCE_TEST_WORKDIR=/tmp, ramfs) the wrong values are produced in RamInode::create, kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/ramfs/fs.rs:931-970: line 945 does `let (uid, gid) = current_fs_ids();`, and current_fs_ids (same file, 1453-1461) reads only `credentials.fsgid()` with no reference to any parent, then lines 946-954 hand that gid and the caller's `mode` verbatim to RamInode::new_dir. `self` at line 945 IS the parent directory inode -- its own metadata is locked and mutated 16 lines later at 961-967 -- so the parent's mode and gid are in hand and simply never consulted. ext2 duplicates the same defect independently in Ext2::create_inode, kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/ext2/fs.rs:382-409, whose lines 394-406 derive (uid, gid) from credentials.fsuid()/fsgid() and ignore the `parent_ino` argument it was given. Neither bit is lost in translation on the way down: InodeMode carries S_ISGID = 0o2000 (kernel/src/fs/file/inode_attr/mode.rs:12) so the from_bits_truncate in sys_mkdirat (kernel/src/syscall/mkdir.rs:34-37) preserves it, and ext2's FilePerm is an unfiltered u16 wrapper (ext2/inode/mod.rs:102-114). The VFS layer above both is a pure pass-through: DirDentry::create (kernel/src/fs/vfs/path/dentry.rs:399-414) forwards `mode` unchanged to `self.inode.create(...)` at line 406, and its sibling DirDentry::mknod (606-622) does the same at line 614. Decisive negative evidence: grepping S_ISGID and has_set_gid across kernel/src/fs/ and kernel/src/syscall/ yields exactly one non-definition use, the hardlink CAP_FOWNER check at kernel/src/fs/vfs/path/mod.rs:306-308. Nothing in the kernel reads a parent's S_ISGID for inheritance, and nothing clears S_ISGID either. I explicitly ruled out the competing hypothesis that setup() silently lost the bit on the parent (which would produce the identical 2 failures): ramfs set_mode stores the full mode verbatim into inode_meta.mode (ramfs/fs.rs:855-860) and set_group/set_owner touch only gid/uid (866-882), so chmod 02777 followed by chown keeps S_ISGID on the parent -- there is a real S_ISGID to inherit and creation ignores it.
invariant: When a new inode is created in a directory that has S_ISGID set, the new inode takes that directory's group id rather than the creating process's fsgid, unconditionally and regardless of the creator's group membership or capabilities; and if the new inode is itself a directory it additionally takes S_ISGID, so the property propagates down the subtree. If the new inode is not a directory it must not gain S_ISGID, and an explicitly requested S_ISGID must be stripped unless the creator is a member of the resulting group or holds CAP_FSETID. When the parent does not have S_ISGID, the new inode takes the creator's fsgid and no setgid bit. The new inode's uid is always the creator's fsuid in every case.
owning_layer: VFS, above the filesystem: the inode-creation path in kernel/src/fs/vfs/path/dentry.rs -- DirDentry::create (399-414) and DirDentry::mknod (606-622), reached from Path::new_fs_child / Path::mknod / Path::create_tmpfile in kernel/src/fs/vfs/path/mod.rs:68-90 and 649-652. This is the layer that already holds both operands of the rule (the parent inode as self.inode, and the requested mode) and it is the only place that sees every filesystem and every caller. Asterinas has no equivalent of Linux's inode_init_owner helper, and its trait boundary does not line up with Linux's: Asterinas's Inode::create/mknod signature (kernel/src/fs/vfs/fs_apis/inode.rs:411-425) takes only (name, type_, mode) and leaves each filesystem to invent the owner ids from current credentials, which is precisely why the rule went missing twice over. Six filesystems implement create (ramfs, ext2, exfat, virtiofs, devpts, overlayfs), so pushing the rule down into the filesystems means writing it six times and being wrong in four of them by default; that is the argument for owning it at the VFS create/mknod layer.
linux_reference: Linux enforces this in inode_init_owner() in fs/inode.c -- a VFS-provided helper that takes the parent (`const struct inode *dir`) explicitly: it sets the fsuid, then `if (dir && dir->i_mode & S_ISGID) { inode->i_gid = dir->i_gid; if (S_ISDIR(mode)) mode |= S_ISGID; else if ((mode & (S_ISGID|S_IXGRP)) == (S_ISGID|S_IXGRP) && !in_group_or_capable(...)) mode &= ~S_ISGID; } else inode_fsgid_set(inode, idmap);`. The rule therefore lives in VFS, above any filesystem, and individual filesystems only call the helper from their create/mkdir/mknod/symlink inode operations (ramfs via ramfs_get_inode, ext4 via __ext4_new_inode, and so on) -- so a filesystem cannot get the policy wrong on its own. CAVEAT ON EVIDENCE: this container has no kernel source and all web reads were blocked by the sandbox (man7.org, elixir.bootlin.com, git.kernel.org, raw.githubusercontent.com and www.kernel.org all refused), so the quoted body is from knowledge, not read this run. It is corroborated empirically rather than left as an assertion: my host probe measured all five branches above (dir inherits + gains S_ISGID, non-dir inherits gid but not the bit, explicitly-requested S_ISGID stripped for a non-member creator, fifo behaves like a file, non-S_ISGID parent falls back to fsgid), and the fact that mkdir, creat and mknod all obey one identical rule is itself evidence it is implemented once above the per-syscall and per-filesystem paths rather than separately in each.
other_callers: Not just mkdir. Every user-facing creation entry point funnels through the same two unpatched VFS methods and is affected identically: sys_mkdirat (kernel/src/syscall/mkdir.rs:38), open(O_CREAT) (kernel/src/syscall/open.rs:115), sys_mknodat for regular files, char/block devices, fifos and sockets (kernel/src/syscall/mknod.rs:48,51,54,57,60), sys_symlink* (kernel/src/syscall/symlink.rs:44), open(O_TMPFILE) via Path::create_tmpfile (kernel/src/syscall/open.rs:149, which in Linux also passes dir to inode_init_owner so gid inheritance applies even with no directory entry), and AF_UNIX bind (kernel/src/net/socket/unix/ns/path.rs:51). Both filesystems the conformance suite exercises are wrong: ramfs (the /tmp workdir this test uses) and ext2 (CONFORMANCE_TEST_WORKDIR=/ext2). exfat, virtiofs and devpts share the same trait boundary and have no inheritance either. Kernel-internal callers that create nodes under /dev and /dev/pts (kernel/src/device/mod.rs:151,155, kernel/src/device/pty/mod.rs:30,41, kernel/src/device/shm.rs:23, kernel/src/fs/rootfs.rs:77-101) run as root in parents without S_ISGID, so they are unaffected in practice. The suite reaches the same defect through more than mkdir02 -- any test asserting setgid-directory semantics for open/creat/mknod hits it -- so a fix confined to sys_mkdirat would turn this test green and leave the invariant violated on five other syscalls.
suggested_direction: Add the missing rule once at the VFS create/mknod layer instead of in each filesystem. Concretely: introduce an Asterinas counterpart of inode_init_owner -- a helper that takes the parent inode plus the requested InodeType and InodeMode and returns the (uid, gid, mode) the new inode must start with -- and call it from DirDentry::create (dentry.rs:406), DirDentry::mknod (dentry.rs:614) and the create_tmpfile path (path/mod.rs:87). Because the gid is currently invented below the boundary, the computed owner has to be conveyed downward, which means extending Inode::create / mknod / create_tmpfile (fs_apis/inode.rs:411-425) to accept the resolved (uid, gid) alongside mode; that also lets ramfs's current_fs_ids (ramfs/fs.rs:1453-1461) and ext2's inline credentials block (ext2/fs.rs:394-406) be deleted rather than duplicated, removing the source of the divergence. Implement all four branches of the invariant, not just the two mkdir02 checks. Traps measured on the host that a fix must not break: a non-directory created in an S_ISGID parent inherits the gid but must NOT gain S_ISGID; an explicitly requested S_ISGID on a non-directory must be stripped when the creator is neither in the resulting group nor CAP_FSETID-capable; a parent without S_ISGID must keep using the creator's fsgid; and gid inheritance itself takes no permission check, so do not gate it on group membership. CapSet::FSETID and the existing has_set_gid()/is_group_executable() helpers (mode.rs:81-83, 57-59) are already available. Since the same rule is missing in ext2, a fix at this layer should be verified against both the default /tmp (ramfs) run that verify will exercise and CONFORMANCE_TEST_WORKDIR=/ext2.
